農業部食農教育資訊整合平臺 – 豆花凝膠機制的介紹

base.tips: Douhua is soy milk set with a coagulant and nothing else — no acid, no salt, no preservative — so it inherits soy milk’s risk profile. The CFS tells shops selling their own soy milk to clear stock within a day of production and consumers to refrigerate it at 4 °C or below immediately. Keep the syrup separate; a bowl already sweetened and topped will not keep.

Not a counter food. Hot douhua may be held above 60 °C; cold douhua must be at 4 °C or below. The gap between the two is where Bacillus cereus grows, and the spores survive the boiling of the soy milk.
Freezing wrecks the curd — it turns spongy and weeps. This is deliberate in 凍豆腐 but ruins douhua.

sourceRefs.name: National Center for Home Food Preservation – Packaging and Storing Dried Foods
香港食物安全中心 – 食物安全五要點：貯存

base.tips: Sealed, cool, dry and dark. The failure mode is not bacteria but rancidity — these are oily fish, and the give-away is a sharp paint-like smell and a yellow-brown cast on what should be silver.
Better than the cupboard in a warm or humid kitchen. Keep the bag sealed so the fish do not perfume the milk.
The usual Japanese advice for 煮干し once opened: freeze it, and use straight from frozen for dashi.

sourceRefs.name: National Center for Home Food Preservation – Packaging and Storing Dried Foods

subtitle: whole pods — ancho, guajillo, pasilla, chipotle, árbol

base.tips: Cool, dry and dark, in a sealed glass jar. NCHFP: dried vegetables keep about half as long as dried fruit, and dried fruit runs 1 year at 60 °F but only 6 months at 80 °F — so a warm kitchen halves the figure again. Pods should still bend without snapping; brittle, faded, dusty-smelling chiles have lost their aroma even if they are safe.

Sealed in a bag in the freezer, dried pods keep their colour and perfume far longer than in a cupboard, and freezing also settles any insect eggs that came in with them. Bring them to room temperature before opening the bag so they do not pick up condensation.

names.en: Dried chiles (whole pods — ancho, guajillo, pasilla, chipotle, árbol)
names.es: Dried chiles (whole pods — ancho, guajillo, pasilla, chipotle, árbol)

subtitle: 冬粉 / mung bean vermicelli, dry

fromPurchase.tips: Mung-bean starch noodles are almost pure dried starch and keep for a long time in a sealed bag in a dry cupboard. Soaked or cooked they become a wet starch food and belong in the fridge.

afterOpening.tips: Reseal; the bundles are hygroscopic and go cloudy and soft in a damp kitchen.

names.en: Glass noodles, dried (冬粉 / mung bean vermicelli, dry)
names.es: Glass noodles, dried (冬粉 / mung bean vermicelli, dry)

sourceRefs.name: NCHFP – Packaging and Storing Dried Foods
Ohioline (Ohio State) HYG-5401 – Pantry Food Storage

base.tips: NCHFP gives dried vegetables about 6 months at 60 °F and 3 months at 80 °F; Ohio State gives dried vegetables a year at 70 °F. Airtight and dark — light bleaches the colour out.

afterOpening.tips: Sealed. Soak in cold water and rinse well before cooking, and use the soaked buds the same day.

fromPurchase.tips: Dried rice vermicelli is shelf-stable purely because it has been dried; keep it in the sealed bag in a dry, ventilated cupboard away from the stove. Once soaked or cooked it becomes a wet rice product and must be refrigerated.

afterOpening.tips: Reseal tightly — the strands are brittle and hygroscopic, and damp bundles mould from the inside.

names.en: Rice vermicelli, dried (米粉 / bee hoon, dry)
names.es: Rice vermicelli, dried (米粉 / bee hoon, dry)

sourceRefs.name: National Center for Home Food Preservation – Packaging and Storing Dried Foods
香港食物安全中心 – 食物安全五要點：貯存

base.tips: Airtight, cool, dry and dark. Conpoy is drier and less oily than dried shrimp, so it keeps longer, but it is expensive enough that most households refrigerate or freeze it anyway. A white bloom of amino-acid crystals is normal; fuzzy grey or green mould is not.
Sealed jar in the fridge is the standard Hong Kong practice for good conpoy.
Freeze the sealed jar; bring it to room temperature before opening so condensation does not settle on the scallops.

sourceRefs.name: National Center for Home Food Preservation – Packaging and Storing Dried Foods
香港食物安全中心 – 食物安全五要點：貯存

base.tips: Airtight jar in a cool, dry, dark cupboard. Hong Kong's CFS rule for goods that need no refrigeration is a cool dry spot in a sealed or covered container. Check the jar often: dried shrimp that has picked up moisture goes tacky, then musty, then mouldy.
Most Chinese kitchens keep 蝦米 in the fridge rather than the cupboard, and in a humid climate that is the sensible choice — it slows the oil going rancid and keeps pantry moths out.
Double-bag it; the smell transfers to everything else in the freezer.

sourceRefs.name: 全国乾麺協同組合連合会 – 表示等のガイドライン（乾めん類及び手延べ干しめん）

subtitle: 干しそば, dry buckwheat noodles

fromPurchase.tips: Same rule as other Japanese dried noodles: 直射日光及び高温多湿を避け保存. Buckwheat flour carries more oil than wheat, so a hot cupboard turns dried soba stale-smelling long before it is unsafe — buy small packs.

afterOpening.tips: Airtight, away from anything aromatic; the federation's guideline specifically warns about smell transfer.

names.en: Dried soba noodles (干しそば, dry buckwheat noodles)
names.es: Dried soba noodles (干しそば, dry buckwheat noodles)

sourceRefs.name: 香港食物安全中心 – 豆腐：大豆製成的傳統素食

base.tips: Despite the name, 豆干 is not a dry food — it is pressed, still-moist bean curd and spoils like fresh tofu. Keep it at 4 °C or below, sealed, and use the printed date. Marinated and braised versions go slimy on the surface first; discard at the first sour smell.
Freezes better than fresh tofu because it holds less water. Slice or shred before freezing.

names.en: Dried tofu (pressed bean curd, 豆干)
names.es: Dried tofu (pressed bean curd, 豆干)

sourceRefs.name: 全国乾麺協同組合連合会 – 表示等のガイドライン（乾めん類及び手延べ干しめん）

fromPurchase.tips: The 全国乾麺協同組合連合会 labelling guideline tells members to print 直射日光及び高温多湿を避け保存 — keep out of direct sun, heat and damp — and to warn on-pack that dried noodles pick up strong smells, so store them away from spices, soap and detergent. Dried noodles carry no preservative; their keeping quality is entirely the low moisture.

afterOpening.tips: Reseal or decant into an airtight jar. At roughly 12% moisture they will mould or attract pantry insects in a humid kitchen.

names.en: Dried udon noodles (干しうどん, dry)
names.es: Dried udon noodles (干しうどん, dry)

sourceRefs.name: National Center for Home Food Preservation – Packaging and Storing Dried Foods

subtitle: yuba / bean curd sticks, 腐竹

base.tips: Store the brittle dry sticks or sheets in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark cupboard. NCHFP puts recommended storage of dried foods generally at 4 months to 1 year, shorter the warmer the room. Any softness, musty smell or visible mould means it has picked up moisture — throw it out.
Freezing in a sealed bag protects the oil-rich sheets from going rancid in a warm kitchen.

names.en: Dried tofu skin (yuba / bean curd sticks, 腐竹)
names.es: Dried tofu skin (yuba / bean curd sticks, 腐竹)

base.tips: Refrigeration time applies to prepared product.
Do not refrigerate.

names.zh: 乾燥填餡麵包粉（市售包裝）

fromPurchase.tips: Uncooked pearls are dried cassava starch and keep well sealed in a dry cupboard. They harden and crack with age — old pearls never soften properly no matter how long you boil them, which is a texture failure rather than a safety one.

afterOpening.tips: Reseal tightly; damp pearls fuse into a solid lump and can mould.

sourceRefs.name: New Mexico State University Extension E-118 – Storing Food Safely
National Center for Home Food Preservation – Freezing Garlic-in-Oil

subtitle: legs slow-cooked and stored under their own fat

base.tips: A retorted tin or jar bought off an ambient shelf is shelf-stable to its date — that is a commercial sterilisation, not the fat. A crock of home-made confit is not, and this is where the tradition and the modern kitchen part company. Meat submerged under a fat seal is a low-acid food in an anaerobic environment, which is the classic setting for Clostridium botulinum, and NCHFP's rule for foods held under oil at room temperature is that they belong in the refrigerator. The old farmhouse practice relied on a cold stone cellar, a heavy salt cure and a short season; a warm modern kitchen supplies none of those.

fromPurchase.tips: An unopened chilled pack keeps to its printed date at or below 4 °C. Home-made confit, salted overnight, cooked slowly in fat, then packed into a sterile jar and covered completely with strained fat with no air pockets, keeps for weeks in the refrigerator — but no agency publishes a number for it, so this record will not invent one. Keep it cold, keep it covered, and use your nose.

afterOpening.tips: Break the fat seal and the clock resets, exactly as with rillettes. What is underneath is a cooked meat dish: 3 to 4 days at or below 4 °C, New Mexico State's figure. Lifting a leg out and smoothing the fat back over the rest restores the look of a seal but not the seal itself — the fat has been broken, contaminated and re-set over a surface that has met a spoon and the air.

base.tips: New Mexico State gives cooked meat dishes 2 to 3 months frozen. Freeze the legs individually with a good coat of fat on them; the fat is excellent protection against freezer burn.

names.en: Duck confit (legs slow-cooked and stored under their own fat)
names.es: Duck confit (legs slow-cooked and stored under their own fat)

names.ja: 若鴨（丸ごと・家鴨／野鴨）

zh.name: 整隻小鴨（家鴨或野鴨）
zh.summary: 整隻小鴨是年輕的鴨，家養或野生皆有，以厚實的皮下脂肪和濃郁的深色肉受到喜愛。生肉在 4°C 以下冷藏，從購買日起只能放 1～2 天；放 −18°C 冷凍約 6 個月，比雞短，因為鴨油比較快酸敗。
zh.pantry: 生鴨肉絕對不能放室溫。和所有禽肉一樣可能帶有沙門氏菌和曲狀桿菌，在 4～60°C 的危險溫度帶會快速繁殖，室溫放超過 2 小時（氣溫超過 32°C 時 1 小時）就要丟棄。打獵帶回的野鴨要盡快處理乾淨並冷藏或冷凍。
zh.fridge: 連包裝放在盤子上、置於冰箱最下層，維持 4°C 以下，並放在所有即食食品的下方，購買後 1～2 天內烹調。想要皮脆，可以把表面拍乾、在皮上戳孔（不要刺到肉），最後一天不加蓋放在架上冷藏——但仍要在 1～2 天的期限內。
zh.freezer: 鴨的脂肪含量高，所以冷凍品質期限只有約 6 個月，而不像瘦的雞可以放一年；在 −18°C 下安全上可以無限期保存。用保鮮膜貼緊，再包鋁箔或裝進大冷凍袋，把空氣完全擠出，並標註重量和日期。
zh.thawing: 放盤子上冷藏解凍，每 2 公斤約 24 小時，一般大小的鴨要一天以上。裝密封袋泡冷水、每 30 分鐘換水比較快，但解凍後要立刻烹調。絕對不要在室溫解凍鴨肉。整隻鴨要烤到大腿最厚處 74°C。
spoilage: 一打開包裝就聞到酸味、硫磺味或阿摩尼亞味
鴨皮黏滑、發黏
肉色變灰、帶綠或異常暗沉，或脂肪有油耗味
盒底血水變混濁牽絲，或已超過有效日期
tips: 戳孔只戳皮不刺肉，油才逼得出來、皮才會脆。
逼出來的鴨油裝罐冷藏，拿來烤馬鈴薯非常好吃。
買回來一兩天內就冷凍，鴨油比雞油更快酸敗。
野鴨可以先在冰箱用鹽水泡一下，有助於去除血水。

faq.q: 整隻鴨可以冷凍嗎？
faq.a: 可以，放 −18°C 冷凍：安全上無限期，但品質以約 6 個月為佳，因為脂肪含量高會縮短風味期限。

faq.q: 生鴨肉放冰箱可以放多久？
faq.a: 在 4°C 以下冷藏，從購買日起只有 1～2 天。

faq.q: 為什麼鴨的冷凍期限比雞短？
faq.a: 鴨的脂肪多很多，脂肪在冷凍庫裡會氧化酸敗，而瘦肉可以維持品質更久。

en.name: Whole duckling (domestic or wild)
en.summary: A whole duckling is a young duck, either farmed or wild, prized for its thick fat layer and rich dark meat. Raw, it keeps only 1–2 days in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below from the day of purchase, and about 6 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F) — less than chicken because duck fat turns rancid sooner.
en.pantry: Raw duck must never be kept at room temperature. Like all poultry it can carry salmonella and campylobacter, which multiply quickly in the danger zone between 4 °C and 60 °C (40 °F and 140 °F), so discard a bird left out for more than 2 hours — 1 hour above 32 °C (90 °F). Wild duck brought home from a hunt should be cleaned and chilled or frozen as fast as possible.
en.fridge: Store the duck in its packaging on a tray on the bottom shelf at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, below all ready-to-eat food, and cook it within 1–2 days of purchase. To get crisp skin, pat it dry, prick the skin without piercing the meat and leave it uncovered on a rack in the fridge for the last day — still within that 1–2 day window.
en.freezer: Duck's high fat content is why the freezer window is about 6 months for good quality, rather than the year you get with a lean chicken; at −18 °C (0 °F) it stays safe indefinitely. Wrap the bird closely in plastic and then foil or a large freezer bag, press out all the air, and label with the weight and date.
en.thawing: Thaw in the fridge on a tray, about 24 hours per 2 kg — a typical duckling needs a full day or more. Cold water in a sealed bag changed every 30 minutes is faster but requires immediate cooking. Never thaw duck on the counter. Cook whole duck to 74 °C (165 °F) in the thickest part of the thigh.
spoilage: Sour, sulphurous or ammonia-like smell as soon as the pack is opened
Slimy or sticky skin
Grey, green or unusually dull colour in the meat, or fat that smells rancid
Cloudy, ropey liquid in the tray, or a passed use-by date
tips: Prick the skin, not the meat, so fat renders out and the skin crisps.
Save the rendered duck fat in a jar in the fridge — it is superb for roast potatoes.
Freeze within a day or two of purchase; duck fat goes rancid faster than chicken fat.
Wild duck benefits from a soak in salted water in the fridge to draw out blood.

faq.q: Can you freeze a whole duck?
faq.a: Yes, at −18 °C (0 °F): safe indefinitely but best quality for about 6 months, because the high fat content shortens quality life.

faq.q: How long does raw duck last in the fridge?
faq.a: Only 1–2 days from the day of purchase at 4 °C (40 °F) or below.

faq.q: Why does duck freeze for less time than chicken?
faq.a: Duck carries far more fat, and fat oxidizes and turns rancid in the freezer while lean meat stays acceptable much longer.

ja.name: 若鴨（丸ごと・家鴨／野鴨）
ja.summary: 丸ごとの若鴨は、家禽でも野生でも、厚い皮下脂肪とこくのある赤身が特徴です。生の状態では4℃以下の冷蔵で購入日から1〜2日、−18℃の冷凍で約6か月。鶏より短いのは、鴨の脂の酸化が早いためです。
ja.pantry: 生の鴨を常温に置くことはできません。ほかの家禽と同様サルモネラやカンピロバクターを持つことがあり、4〜60℃の危険温度帯では急速に増えます。室温に2時間以上（気温32℃以上なら1時間以上）置いたものは処分してください。狩猟で得た野鴨は、できるだけ早く処理して冷蔵または冷凍します。
ja.fridge: 包装のままトレーにのせ、冷蔵庫の最下段で4℃以下を保ち、そのまま食べる食品より下に置いて、購入から1〜2日以内に調理します。皮をパリッとさせたい場合は、表面を拭き、肉まで刺さないよう皮にだけ穴をあけ、最後の1日を網にのせて覆わずに冷蔵します（1〜2日の枠内で）。
ja.freezer: 脂が多いため、冷凍の品質目安は約6か月で、赤身の鶏の1年ほどにはなりません（−18℃なら安全面では長期間保存できます）。ラップで密着させ、ホイルか大きめの保存袋で包んで空気を完全に抜き、重量と日付をラベルに書いておきましょう。
ja.thawing: トレーにのせて冷蔵庫で解凍し、2kgあたり約24時間。一般的な大きさの鴨で1日以上かかります。密閉袋で冷水解凍（30分ごとに水替え）は早いですが、解凍後すぐ調理が必要です。常温解凍は厳禁。丸ごとの場合はももの厚い部分が74℃になるまで加熱します。
spoilage: パックを開けた瞬間に酸っぱいにおい、硫黄臭、アンモニア臭がする
皮がぬめる・べたつく
肉が灰色・緑がかった色・異常にくすんだ色になっている、脂に酸敗臭がある
トレーのドリップが濁って糸を引く、消費期限を過ぎている
tips: 肉ではなく皮にだけ穴をあけると、脂が抜けて皮がパリッとする。
出てきた鴨脂は瓶に入れて冷蔵。じゃがいもを焼くと絶品。
購入後1〜2日で冷凍する。鴨脂は鶏脂より酸化が早い。
野鴨は冷蔵庫で塩水に浸けると血抜きができる。

faq.q: 鴨は丸ごと冷凍できますか？
faq.a: できます。−18℃で安全面では長期間ですが、脂が多いため品質の目安は約6か月です。

faq.q: 生の鴨は冷蔵庫で何日もちますか？
faq.a: 4℃以下で購入日から1〜2日だけです。

faq.q: 鴨の冷凍期間が鶏より短いのはなぜ？
faq.a: 鴨は脂がはるかに多く、その脂が冷凍中に酸化して風味が落ちるためです。赤身中心の肉のほうが長く品質を保てます。

es.name: Pato joven entero (doméstico o silvestre)
es.summary: Un pato joven entero, de granja o silvestre, se aprecia por su gruesa capa de grasa y su carne oscura y sabrosa. Crudo dura solo 1–2 días en el refrigerador a 4 °C (40 °F) o menos desde la compra, y unos 6 meses en el congelador a −18 °C (0 °F), menos que el pollo porque la grasa de pato se enrancia antes.
es.pantry: El pato crudo nunca debe guardarse a temperatura ambiente. Como toda ave puede portar salmonela y campylobacter, que se multiplican rápido en la zona de peligro entre 4 °C y 60 °C (40 °F y 140 °F): desecha un ave que lleve más de 2 horas fuera —1 hora por encima de 32 °C (90 °F)—. El pato silvestre traído de una cacería debe limpiarse y enfriarse o congelarse cuanto antes.
es.fridge: Guarda el pato en su envase sobre una bandeja en el estante inferior a 4 °C (40 °F) o menos, por debajo de todos los alimentos listos para comer, y cocínalo en 1–2 días desde la compra. Para una piel crujiente, sécalo, pincha la piel sin llegar a la carne y déjalo destapado sobre una rejilla el último día, siempre dentro de esa ventana de 1–2 días.
es.freezer: Su alto contenido graso explica que el plazo en congelador sea de unos 6 meses de buena calidad, en vez del año de un pollo magro; a −18 °C (0 °F) se mantiene seguro indefinidamente. Envuélvelo pegado con film y luego con aluminio o una bolsa grande, saca todo el aire y etiqueta con peso y fecha.
es.thawing: Descongélalo en el refrigerador sobre una bandeja, unas 24 horas por cada 2 kg: un pato normal necesita un día o más. El agua fría en bolsa cerrada, cambiada cada 30 minutos, es más rápida pero obliga a cocinar de inmediato. Nunca lo descongeles en la encimera. Cocina el pato entero hasta 74 °C (165 °F) en la parte más gruesa del muslo.
spoilage: Olor agrio, sulfuroso o a amoníaco nada más abrir el paquete
Piel viscosa o pegajosa
Carne gris, verdosa o anormalmente apagada, o grasa con olor rancio
Líquido turbio y filante en la bandeja, o fecha de consumo vencida
tips: Pincha la piel, no la carne, para que la grasa salga y la piel quede crujiente.
Guarda la grasa de pato en un frasco en el refrigerador: es magnífica para asar papas.
Congélalo uno o dos días tras la compra; su grasa se enrancia antes que la de pollo.
El pato silvestre mejora con un remojo en agua salada dentro del refrigerador para sacar la sangre.

faq.q: ¿Se puede congelar un pato entero?
faq.a: Sí, a −18 °C (0 °F): seguro indefinidamente pero con la mejor calidad unos 6 meses, porque su grasa acorta la vida útil.

faq.q: ¿Cuánto dura el pato crudo en el refrigerador?
faq.a: Solo 1–2 días desde el día de compra a 4 °C (40 °F) o menos.

faq.q: ¿Por qué el pato se congela menos tiempo que el pollo?
faq.a: Tiene mucha más grasa, y la grasa se oxida y enrancia en el congelador mientras la carne magra aguanta bastante más.

subtitle: jarred or canned milk caramel
keywords: ドゥルセ・デ・レチェ
ミルクキャラメルクリーム

fromPurchase.tips: Unopened, in a cool dark cupboard. The jar or can is commercially heat-processed and shelf-stable; check the date on the lid. A can that is bulging, leaking or rusted through goes in the bin unopened. Homemade dulce de leche is not shelf-stable and belongs in the fridge from the moment it cools.

afterOpening.tips: Once opened, keep it covered at or below 40 °F (4 °C) and always take it out with a clean spoon — a buttery knife is what turns a jar mouldy. It stiffens to a paste when cold; stand the jar in warm water rather than microwaving it. Decant anything left in an opened can into a glass jar.

names.en: Dulce de leche (jarred or canned milk caramel)
names.es: Dulce de leche (jarred or canned milk caramel)

base.tips: Fresh wheat dough rounds. Keep the stack sealed and lying flat; once air reaches them the edges dry and will not seal. A dried edge is a quality problem — a slimy or sour-smelling stack is a safety one, so discard it.
Freeze flat in the sleeve. Thaw in the fridge, still wrapped, so condensation does not glue the sheets together.

names.en: Dumpling wrappers (fresh gyoza / jiaozi skins, refrigerated)
names.es: Dumpling wrappers (fresh gyoza / jiaozi skins, refrigerated)

sourceRefs.name: 農業部農業知識入口網 – 水果如何保存（榴槤須催熟後才可冷藏）
Philippine Department of Agriculture, Bureau of Agricultural Research – Improving durian shelf life through postharvest strategies

base.tips: Keep a whole, uncut fruit at room temperature until it is ripe. Philippine agricultural research recorded pods splitting 8 to 10 days after harvest in ambient tropical conditions, and the fruit is best eaten before it splits.

Refrigerate only once ripe, and only the flesh, sealed in an airtight container so the aroma does not transfer to everything else. Durian is chilling-sensitive: damage appeared within two weeks at 7 °C, so do not hold a whole fruit cold for long.
Freeze the flesh in portions with the seeds removed. This is how durian is traded internationally, and the texture holds up better than most fruit.

zh.name: 榴槤
zh.summary: 榴槤是東南亞那顆帶刺、氣味出名濃烈的水果，綿密的果肉可以新鮮吃也可以冷凍吃。整顆未剖開的請放室溫約 2 到 5 天催熟；剖開的果肉密封冷藏 3 到 5 天；分份冷凍大約 3 到 6 個月。
zh.pantry: 整顆沒剖開的榴槤該待的地方就是室溫，而且一定要先催熟才能靠近冰箱。菲律賓的農業研究記錄到，在熱帶常溫條件下果實會在採收後 8 到 10 天裂開，而在裂開之前吃最好，所以請打算在買回來 2 到 5 天內剖開。要放在通風處：密閉的廚房、車內或旅館房間會連續好幾天都是榴槤味。
zh.fridge: 熟了才冷藏，而且只冷藏果肉——裝進密封盒放 4°C 以下，3 到 5 天內吃完。這個數字是比照「切開的水果」的一般處理方式，不是榴槤專屬的公布數據。榴槤也怕冷：在 7°C 下兩週內就出現寒害，所以不要把整顆榴槤長期放冰箱。密封盒不是可有可無的，那個香氣一定會鑽進奶油、牛奶和所有沒蓋好的東西裡。
zh.freezer: 冷凍正是榴槤國際貿易的形式，而且它的口感比大多數水果更耐凍。去籽、分份、裝雙層袋並擠出空氣；−18°C 下大約 3 到 6 個月是商業上採用的範圍，不是官方數字。很多人偏好半解凍狀態吃，口感像冰淇淋。
zh.thawing: 取一份放冷藏解凍，或直接從冷凍庫拿出來半解凍吃，冷凍榴槤通常就是這樣上桌的。不要放室溫解凍，解凍過的果肉也不要回凍。
spoilage: 在原本的濃烈氣味之外，出現酒味、酸味或油耗味
果肉不再綿密，變得水水的、發灰或鬆軟
外殼裂開並滲出液體，或裡面看得到黴
整顆拿起來輕、搖起來會響，表示已經乾掉
tips: 整顆放室溫催熟，硬的榴槤絕對不要冰
墊報紙剖開並戴手套，那些刺是真的會刺傷人
要冷藏或冷凍的一律裝雙層袋
按一次吃得完的份量冷凍，因為不能回凍

faq.q: 榴槤可以冷凍嗎？
faq.a: 可以，這正是它在全球流通的形式。去籽分份裝雙層袋，約 3 到 6 個月，半解凍吃最好。

faq.q: 剖開的榴槤放冰箱可以放多久？
faq.a: 裝密封盒放 4°C 以下約 3 到 5 天。一定要密封好，不然整個冰箱都會是味道。

faq.q: 榴槤需要冷藏嗎？
faq.a: 催熟之後才需要。整顆硬的要放室溫，長時間低溫會造成寒害。

en.name: Durian
en.summary: Durian is the spiny, famously pungent Southeast Asian fruit whose custardy flesh is eaten fresh or frozen. Keep a whole uncut fruit at room temperature for about 2 to 5 days until ripe, refrigerate the opened flesh sealed for 3 to 5 days, and freeze portioned flesh for roughly 3 to 6 months.
en.pantry: A whole, uncut durian belongs at room temperature until it is ripe, and it must be ripened before it goes anywhere near a fridge. Philippine agricultural research recorded pods splitting 8 to 10 days after harvest in tropical ambient conditions, and the fruit eats best before it splits, so plan on opening it within about 2 to 5 days of buying. Keep it somewhere ventilated: a closed kitchen, a car or a hotel room will smell of durian for days.
en.fridge: Refrigerate only once the fruit is ripe, and only the flesh — seal it in an airtight container at 4 °C (40 °F) or below and use it within 3 to 5 days. That figure follows the general handling of cut fruit rather than a durian-specific published number. Durian is also chilling-sensitive: damage appeared within two weeks at 7 °C, so do not park a whole fruit in the fridge for a long stay. The airtight box is not optional, because the aroma will find its way into butter, milk and everything uncovered.
en.freezer: Freezing is how durian is traded internationally, and the texture survives better than most fruit. Remove the seeds, portion the flesh, double-bag it and press out the air; roughly 3 to 6 months at −18 °C (0 °F) is the range used commercially rather than an official figure. Many people prefer it eaten semi-frozen, when it has the texture of ice cream.
en.thawing: Thaw a portion in the fridge, or eat it semi-frozen straight from the freezer, which is how frozen durian is usually served. Do not thaw it on the counter, and do not refreeze thawed flesh.
spoilage: Alcoholic, sour or rancid note over and above the normal pungency
Flesh gone watery, grey or slack rather than creamy
Split shell with weeping liquid or visible mould inside
A fruit that feels light for its size and rattles, meaning it has dried out
tips: Ripen it whole at room temperature; never chill a hard durian
Open it over newspaper and wear gloves — the spines are genuinely sharp
Double-bag anything you refrigerate or freeze
Freeze in single-serving portions; you cannot refreeze it

faq.q: Can you freeze durian?
faq.a: Yes, and it is how the fruit is traded worldwide. Deseed, portion and double-bag it for roughly 3 to 6 months, and eat it semi-frozen.

faq.q: How long does opened durian last in the fridge?
faq.a: About 3 to 5 days in an airtight container at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. Seal it well or the whole fridge will smell.

faq.q: Should durian be refrigerated?
faq.a: Only after it has ripened. A whole hard fruit needs room temperature, and prolonged cold causes chilling damage.

ja.name: ドリアン
ja.summary: ドリアンはとげに覆われ、強烈な香りで知られる東南アジアの果実で、クリーム状の果肉を生でも冷凍でも食べます。丸ごとは常温で2〜5日ほど置いて追熟させ、開けた果肉は密閉して冷蔵で3〜5日、小分けにして冷凍でおよそ3〜6か月です。
ja.pantry: 丸ごと切っていないドリアンの居場所は常温で、冷蔵庫に入れる前に必ず追熟させます。フィリピンの農業研究では、熱帯の常温下で収穫から8〜10日で果実が裂けると記録されており、裂ける前が最もおいしいので、購入から2〜5日で開ける前提で考えてください。風通しのよい場所に置くこと。閉め切った台所や車内、ホテルの部屋は何日もドリアンの香りが残ります。
ja.fridge: 冷蔵は熟してから、しかも果肉だけにします。密閉容器に入れて4℃以下で3〜5日以内に。この数字はカットフルーツ一般の扱いに従ったもので、ドリアン固有の公表値ではありません。ドリアンは低温にも弱く、7℃では2週間以内に障害が現れたと報告されています。丸ごとを長く冷蔵しないでください。密閉は必須で、香りはバターや牛乳、ふたのないものすべてに移ります。
ja.freezer: 冷凍はドリアンの国際的な流通形態そのもので、多くの果物より食感がよく残ります。種を除いて小分けにし、二重の袋に入れて空気を抜きます。−18℃で3〜6か月は商業的に使われる範囲で、公的な数字ではありません。半解凍でアイスクリームのような食感を楽しむ人が多いです。
ja.thawing: 1回分を冷蔵庫で解凍するか、冷凍庫から出して半解凍のまま食べます。冷凍ドリアンはたいていその食べ方です。常温解凍と再冷凍は避けてください。
spoilage: 本来の強い香りに加えてアルコール臭・酸臭・古い油のにおい
果肉がクリーム状でなく水っぽい、灰色っぽい、だれている
殻が裂けて液が出ている、内部にカビが見える
見た目より軽く、振ると音がする（乾いている）
tips: 丸ごと常温で追熟させる。硬いうちに冷やさない
新聞紙を敷き、手袋をして開ける（とげは本当に鋭い）
冷蔵・冷凍するものは必ず二重に包む
1回分ずつ冷凍する（再冷凍はできません）

faq.q: ドリアンは冷凍できますか？
faq.a: できます。世界的にも冷凍で流通しています。種を除いて小分けにし二重の袋で3〜6か月、半解凍で食べるのがおすすめです。

faq.q: 開けたドリアンは冷蔵庫でどのくらい持ちますか？
faq.a: 密閉容器で4℃以下なら3〜5日です。しっかり密閉しないと庫内全体が香ります。

faq.q: ドリアンは冷蔵が必要ですか？
faq.a: 追熟してからだけです。硬い丸ごとは常温に置き、長時間の低温は低温障害を招きます。

es.name: Durián
es.summary: El durián es la fruta espinosa del Sudeste Asiático, célebre por su olor, cuya pulpa cremosa se come fresca o congelada. Mantén la fruta entera a temperatura ambiente unos 2 a 5 días hasta que madure, refrigera la pulpa abierta bien cerrada de 3 a 5 días y congélala en porciones unos 3 a 6 meses.
es.pantry: Un durián entero y sin abrir debe estar a temperatura ambiente hasta madurar, y hay que madurarlo antes de acercarlo a la nevera. La investigación agrícola filipina registró que las cápsulas se abren de 8 a 10 días tras la cosecha en condiciones tropicales, y la fruta está mejor antes de agrietarse, así que cuenta con abrirlo entre 2 y 5 días tras la compra. Déjalo en un sitio ventilado: una cocina cerrada, un coche o una habitación olerán a durián durante días.
es.fridge: Refrigéralo solo ya maduro y solo la pulpa: ciérrala en un recipiente hermético a 4 °C (40 °F) o menos y consúmela en 3 a 5 días. Esa cifra sigue el manejo general de la fruta cortada, no un dato publicado para el durián. Además es sensible al frío: a 7 °C aparecieron daños en dos semanas, así que no dejes una fruta entera mucho tiempo en la nevera. El hermético no es opcional: el aroma acaba en la mantequilla, la leche y todo lo destapado.
es.freezer: La congelación es la forma en que el durián se comercializa internacionalmente, y la textura resiste mejor que la de casi cualquier fruta. Quita las semillas, divide la pulpa en porciones, usa doble bolsa y saca el aire; unos 3 a 6 meses a −18 °C (0 °F) es el rango del comercio, no una cifra oficial. Mucha gente lo prefiere semicongelado, con textura de helado.
es.thawing: Descongela una ración en la nevera, o cómelo semicongelado recién sacado, que es como suele servirse. No lo descongeles en la encimera ni recongeles pulpa descongelada.
spoilage: Nota alcohólica, agria o rancia por encima de su olor habitual
Pulpa acuosa, grisácea o flácida en lugar de cremosa
Cáscara abierta que rezuma o moho visible en el interior
Fruta ligera para su tamaño que suena al agitarla: se ha secado
tips: Madúralo entero a temperatura ambiente; nunca enfríes un durián duro
Ábrelo sobre papel y con guantes: las espinas pinchan de verdad
Usa doble bolsa para todo lo que refrigeres o congeles
Congélalo en raciones individuales: no se puede recongelar

faq.q: ¿Se puede congelar el durián?
faq.a: Sí, y así se comercializa en todo el mundo. Sin semillas, en porciones y con doble bolsa, unos 3 a 6 meses; cómelo semicongelado.

faq.q: ¿Cuánto dura el durián abierto en la nevera?
faq.a: Unos 3 a 5 días en recipiente hermético a 4 °C (40 °F) o menos. Ciérralo bien o toda la nevera olerá.

faq.q: ¿Hay que refrigerar el durián?
faq.a: Solo después de madurar. La fruta entera y dura necesita temperatura ambiente, y el frío prolongado la daña.
